Why people have raged about Cecil the Lion (and other "megafauna")

I am curious what other fellow hunters make of the crazed rage about Cecil the lion. And I am concerned that this behavior/reaction may turn into a blind witch hunt wih zero consideration for the conservation efforts of hunters. (While at the same time I am irritated that the hunter looks as if he was not being legal which puts all of the ethical and protective hunters in a bad light.)

The article appears biased "The brutal killing of Cecil the lion in Zimbabwe...", from my perspective it appears to be a media hyped overreaction. How did "nature" benefit from all the tweets and facebook likes these past days, I doubt much. Without all the facts people have gone full witch hunt mode mixed with a fair amount of slacktivism. The lion was old (past breeding age), the correct permits where paid for, hunting provides income for very poor communities, and if managed carefully improve ecosystems. I am not pro-trophy hunting and more eat what you kill, but there is need that this type of hunting fills provided it is carefully managed.

I completely agree. I am not sure what the final word was on whether the permits were valid. I think there was some question on that. And if they werent then this guy was setting a terrible example, or at least his PH was. But good luck explaining that to the guy in my social network news feed that just called me a neaderthal. and "less than human, at best" for being a hunter. And I have been "trophy hunting" but I mostly hunt for food for my family and friends.

It might also be worth noting that I have been on safari in Africa. And, without too long an explaination, I have seen what the public and private lands look like where hunting is not allowed or encouraged...and that land is wasteland. Totally ruined with trash, waste, and barren of even the under brush. We never see this sort of ruin in the states except maybe the worst ghettos. Also, plains game get trapped on cattle lands where the farmers only pump water to the surface for their cattle and the fences cut off the wildlife. It is heartbreaking to see the game get trapped and slowly starve and die of thirst. If hunting isnt bringing in money, the wildlife is ignored completely for more profitable land uses. There is no concept of search and rescue for animals, relocation programs, etc except for the high-tourist-traffic parks. Which completely misrepresent what is happening to the wildlife when people are trying to turn a profit without hunting or conservation. It is absolutely fightening.
